text:
incident-bot: paging kayla — high 95th latency on embeddings.europe (eu-west-2) and sudden token surge on /v1/embeddings since 03:02 UTC

kayla: seeing it, joining. where's the telemetry link?

ashok: https://console.redwood.ai/metrics/embeddings?region=eu-west-2 — 95p jumped from 120ms -> 820ms, token/sec 6x baseline. top caller: analytics-heavy-client (key starts with sk-prod-...)

samir: verified. economy-tier routes taking majority of traffic, and fallback to quantized-gpt-embed-xq is failing, so lots of retries swelling load.

jess: paging infra team, possible hot client or misconfiguration at customer side but impact is platform-wide in region.

kayla: OK, live mitigation plan: 1) reduce economy-tier capacity by throttling to 20rps, 2) tighten per-key quota for embeddings (temporary 10k/min), 3) disable batch fallback for embed route to avoid big mem spikes, 4) route new economy requests to quantized-lite variant with lower perf but stable. want ops-bot to run policy changes now.

ops-bot: @kayla received. Confirming run: applyPolicy(policy=eu-west-2-economy-surge-2026, actions=[throttle:20rps, per_key_quota:10000/min, disable:embed_batched_fallback, route_overrides:{economy:/models/quantized-lite-embed}])

kayla: go for it. I will watch error budget and 95p.

ops-bot: executing...

```
# ops-bot output
POST /api/v1/policies/apply
{"policy": "eu-west-2-economy-surge-2026", "status": "in-progress"}
Applied throttle -> 20rps to route /v1/embeddings (economy)
Set per-key quota to 10000/min for embeddings routes
Disabled embed_batched_fallback on routers in eu-west-2
Added route override: economy -> models/quantized-lite-embed
All changes pushed to 6/6 routers
```

infra-bot: rollout completed on all active router pods in eu-west-2. CPU/p95 showing gradual drop.

ashok: immediate metrics: token/sec down 65%, p95 emb down to 240ms from 820ms, error rate stable at 0.9% (was 3.4%). Looks like mitigation working.

samir: seeing degraded quality on some customer evals for economy-tier — acceptable tradeoff? alex-product, any concerns for users?

alex-product: product aware. this affects only economy-tier non-SLA customers and heavy batch embedding jobs. recommend calling out in status page: "temporary reduced throughput and lower-quality embedded variant for economy plan in eu-west-2 to protect platform stability."

jess: agreed. I'll draft a short status update.

kayla: also need to identify heavy key(s). run quick top keys query.

ops-bot: running query: top_api_keys_by_tokens(region=eu-west-2, window=5m)

```
# query output
1) sk-prod-9x4... - 42% of tokens
2) sk-prod-1b2... - 12%
3) internal-analytics - 8%
others <5%
```

kayla: flagged sk-prod-9x4... for emergency soft-throttle — reduce to 200rps and email owner.

ops-bot: applied per-key throttle sk-prod-9x4... -> 200rps. Notifying account team.

ashok: we should capture a replay and request the customer to batch less or spread over time. Also add a short-term quota to internal-analytics.

samir: monitoring for potential collateral impact — check dedicated customers in eu-west-2 not affected. Confirmed dedicated pools unaffected.

jess: status page update posted: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2118001111 — "Mitigation in place: temporary throttles & route override for economy-tier in eu-west-2. No SLA customers affected. Investigating heavy client usage."

alex-product: customer outreach: CS will message affected customers with guidance. Security/compliance: nothing to report.

kayla: plan next steps: 1) keep throttles for 30m, 2) validate p95 < 350ms and error rate <1.5%, 3) identify root cause for burst (client-side vs internal retry loop), 4) prepare rollback playbook. If metrics stable at 30m, gradually relax per-key throttle to 1k rps and lift economy global throttle to 50rps, route back to standard embed model.

ops-bot: scheduled policy rollback check in 30m (2118002911) with automatic alert if p95 or error budget exceed thresholds.

samir: also capturing logs for embed_batched_fallback failure — pushing to /incident/2118001111/artifacts.

jess: great. anyone want to take postmortem? I'll coordinate on incident timeline and customer comms.

kayla: I'll lead the postmortem with samir and ashok. tagging alex-product for customer impact notes.

ashok: one more note: add an alert rule to detect sudden client-key token spikes (delta > 3x in 1m) to reduce time-to-mitigate next time.

alex-product: acknowledged. will include in action items.

kayla: thanks team. keeping the channel open, will update at +10m and +30m. :thumbsup:
